The operator 'fair_probability_mix' combines these inputs via \hat{p}_{\text{fair}} = w \cdot p_{\text{engine}} + (1 - w) \cdot p_{\text{market}}, where w=0.15. This preserves existing ranking orders and composite weights while introducing a calibrated correction. The 'calibration_correction' primitive adjusts for systematic bias by measuring deviation Δp = p_market − p_engine. The 'engine_weight_fitting' primitive determines w via empirical minimization of squared error on historical data, yielding w=0.15. Dualities emerge in that the engine provides independence from stale market data, while the market offers calibration insight. Failure modes include invalid inputs causing fallback behavior, and out-of-time degradation due to temporal drift between training and deployment periods.
